Beyond Networking

Some of the strongest relationships are built while doing meaningful work together—not while exchanging introductions.

18 July 20265 min read
CommunityRelationshipsUCLA

I have never been particularly comfortable with the word networking. It can make relationships sound like something collected rather than something built.

The relationships that have mattered most in my life rarely began with an agenda. They began with shared work: solving a problem, building a project, helping a classmate or showing up repeatedly for a community.

Working across teams at UCLA reinforced something I had experienced throughout my career. Collaboration reveals people in ways introductions cannot. You learn how someone listens, how they respond when plans change, whether they share credit and whether they can be relied upon.

Perhaps the better question is not, ‘How many people did I meet?’ It is, ‘What did we build together?’
